style: Say in a knowledgeable, friendly way, like a museum curator
lines: Hello, art explorers! Artists all over the world make art. Tap a picture on the map and let's go see it!
Tap a picture on the map to visit art from another part of the world.
We got a passport stamp!
This is The Great Wave, from Japan.
This is William the Hippo, from Egypt.
This is the Smiling Figure, from Mexico.
This is an Antelope Headdress, from Mali.
This is Night-Shining White, a horse painting from China.
This is the Dragon Jar, from Korea.
This is a Dish with Two Birds, from Turkey.
This is Wheat Field with Cypresses, painted in France.
This is The Harvesters, from Belgium.
This is a Wearing Blanket, from the Diné, or Navajo, Nation.
This is an Album Quilt, from the United States.
This is a Carved House Post, from New Zealand.
This is the Winged Runner Ear Ornament, from Peru.
This is Young Elephant Eating, from India.
What do you see?
What does it make you think?
What do you wonder about it?
Find the snowy mountain far away. It is Mount Fuji, and it looks tiny!
Find a boat. The people are holding on tight!
Look at the foam on top of the wave. Does it look like fingers or claws?
Find the plants and flowers painted on the hippo. Hippos lived among river plants.
Look at the face. Is William happy, sleepy or grumpy?
Look at the big smile! Can you smile just like this?
Look at the hat. The pattern goes all the way around.
Both arms are up. Is this person waving, dancing or cheering?
Find the long horns reaching up to the sky.
Look for lines carved into the wood. Are they zigzag or straight?
Look at the horse's eye and mane. Is it calm or excited?
The horse is tied to a post. It wants to run free!
Find the red stamps. Each one is the name of someone who owned this painting.
Find the dragon's face. Can you see its whiskers?
Little clouds float around the dragon. Dragons were said to bring the rain.
Look at the scales. Do they look like fish scales?
Find the two birds. What are they doing?
Find the big red flower.
The edge has a pattern that repeats all the way around.
Find the tall dark tree. It looks like a green flame!
Look at the swirly clouds. The paint is thick and bumpy.
The golden wheat bends in the wind.
Find the people eating lunch under the tree.
Someone is taking a nap! Can you find him?
Far away: a village, a church and boats on the water.
Find the zigzag lines.
Find a diamond shape. Can you find another one?
Look at the stripes on the sides.
Find the blue bird.
Find a harp, a music instrument!
Find a basket of flowers. How many can you find?
Look at the face at the top. What shape are the eyes?
Find the spirals carved into the wood.
Find the runner. He has wings and a bird face!
Count the gold balls around the edge.
The elephant holds grass in its trunk. Snack time!
Find the chains around its ankles.
Find the red blanket on its back.
Is the wave about to crash? What do you think happens next?
Why do you think the artist made the hippo blue?
What do you think this person is so happy about?
Why do you think the horns are so long and tall?
How do you think the horse feels? How can you tell?
If this dragon could move, where would it fly?
Which colors did the artist use again and again?
Is it windy in this picture? How do you know?
What would you eat for lunch in this field?
What do the zigzags remind you of?
If our class made a quilt, what would you put on your square?
What do you think this figure is saying to visitors?
Where do you think the runner is going so fast?
Is this elephant big or little? How can you tell?
Make your arms into a big curling wave. Now freeze, like the picture!
Walk slowly like a heavy hippo. Now pretend to swim in the river.
Stand like the figure: arms up, big smile. Hold it!
Leap and bend like an antelope dancing in a field.
Gallop in place like a strong horse. Now toss your head!
Wiggle your whole body like a dragon in the clouds.
Flap your wings like the birds, then perch on a flower.
Sway like wheat in the wind, then swirl like the clouds.
Pretend to cut wheat, stack it, then take a nap in the sun.
Draw a zigzag in the air with your finger. Now a diamond!
Hold hands with a friend, like the squares are sewn together.
Stand tall and proud like the post, guarding the door.
Run in place as fast as you can, then flap your wings!
Swing your arm like a trunk and scoop up some grass.
Try it!
What is the same? What is different?
Think about colors, lines, shapes, animals, people, and what it is made of.
Both have curvy, swirly lines. One is a print, one is a painting.
Both are big animals. One is a sculpture you can walk around, one is a flat painting.
Both are made of cloth and full of patterns. One is woven, one is sewn from squares.
Both are blue and white pottery, from far apart in Asia.
Both show people. One is smiling and dancing; one stands tall and proud.
Both are animals that love to run and leap.
Both are wheat fields in summer, painted 300 years apart!
Both show movement: a runner and a dancing antelope.
Both have birds and flowers. Can you find them?
Every time we visit a work of art, we get a stamp. Tap a stamp to visit again.
